rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/cards.json S7-c096 (lesson L06, misconception 'A t-statistic above 3 proves the predictor is real.'): grade T, basis 'Lab 3 (exact posterior probabilities); Lab 1 (simulation) for the dependence on the number of predictors'
rows.evidence: Re-checked at 4051c1a: cards.json S7-c096 (lesson L06; misconception 'A t-statistic above 3 proves the predictor is real.'): grade T; basis 'Lab 3 (exact posterior probabilities)'; back 'A hurdle controls an error rate over a family of tests; it says nothing certain about one predictor. With a 99% prior probability of the null, t = 3 still leaves the null more likely than not (Lab 3).' The Lab 1 (simulation) clause is gone, so no simulated result is graded T. Derivation: L06.html Theorem 4.2 (T, proved on the page, lines 257-266): for every prior on the alternative B >= e^{-z^2/2} because the integral of phi(z-theta) pi(dtheta) is at most phi(0); hence P(H0|z) >= PO e^{-z^2/2}/(1 + PO e^{-z^2/2}). Spot-check (python, .venv): PO = 0.99/0.01 = 99, z = 3: 99 e^{-4.5} = 1.09982; 1.09982/2.09982 = 0.52383 > 0.5, which is the 0.5238 printed by Lab 3 (run_labs reproduced it; Lab 3 is deterministic, no RNG). The card is therefore T on the page plus an exact lab evaluation (BUILDER_RULES 7 and brief step 7).

rows.check: 2.4-mathematics (the new _invert: derivation and domain)
rows.location: tools/fetch_data.py _invert (lines 203-222 at 7254468); domain: _PLAIN_NUMBER = -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? (line 141)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 765bcb1 (git diff checked); round-22 evidence: Derivation checked line by line. x = Fraction(value), exact; x = 0 is refused (DataError). inv = 1/|x| = q/p exactly, with p = numerator, q = denominator of |x|. lead0 = len(str(q)) - len(str(p)); if q in [10^(n1-1), 10^n1) and p in [10^(n2-1), 10^n2) then inv in (10^(n1-n2-1), 10^(n1-n2+1)), so floor(log10 inv) is lead0-1 or lead0. The branch 'if inv < 10**lead0: lead = lead0-1' therefore gives 10^lead <= inv < 10^(lead+1) (verified in the proof and by the 264,470-input check, which exercises both branches). y = inv/10^(lead-7) lies in [10^7, 10^8); round(y) (Fraction.__round__, half to even, exact) gives digits in [10^7, 10^8]; digits = 10^8 happens only when y >= 10^8 - 1/2, and then digits, lead = 10^7, lead+1 gives 10^(lead+1) exactly, matching the rule 9.99999996 -> 10.000000. Output Decimal(digits).scaleb(lead-7) is exact and plain (:f). Sign: the sign of x is restored; abs() makes lead well defined for negative x. Domain: every accepted value is a terminating decimal, so the only inputs whose inverse is an exact 9-digit tie are x = 0.4096 x 10^-k (the ties 2.44140625 x 10^k), as shown in r16-equiv-I03. Result: the derivation is correct for every plain decimal input.

rows.check: 2.6-mutation (equivalence proof and check: ROUND_HALF_DOWN in place of half to even)
rows.location: tools/fetch_data.py _invert: digits = round(inverse / 10**(lead-7)) replaced by digits = -((1/2 - y).__floor__()) (ceil(y - 1/2))
rows.evidence: unchanged since 765bcb1 (git diff checked); round-22 evidence: Equivalent on every input _invert accepts. Proof: the two rules differ only when y is exactly k + 1/2. Then inv = (2k+1) x 10^(lead-8). For a terminating input x = a/10^b, 10^b/a = inv gives a(2k+1) = 10^(b-lead+8), so (2k+1) divides a power of 10 and is therefore 5^q. Since 10^7 <= k < 10^8, 2k+1 lies in (2x10^7, 2x10^8), which contains 5^11 = 48828125 and no other 5^q. So k = 24414062 is the only exact tie, and its last digit 2 is even: half down and half to even both give 24414062. Check: scratch equiv_invert.py over 264,470 inputs (the tie family 0.4096 x 10^-k, k = -40..40; powers of ten and neighbours; 300,000 random terminating decimals): 'I03_half_down differs on 0 of 264470'. def test_by_isbn_refuses_a_citation_of_another_edition(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    # A 2nd-edition citation is not admitted against the record of the 3rd edition.
    import add_reference
    from refs.parse import parse_source
    from refs.web import Fetcher

    class Record:
        def __init__(self, fetcher: Fetcher) -> None:
            self.fetcher = fetcher

        def edition_record(self, isbn: str, *, use_cache: bool = True) -> tuple[Work, str | None]:
            return work(), "3 edition"

    monkeypatch.setattr(add_reference, "OpenLibrary", Record)

        parse_source("Spivak, Calculus, 2nd ed. (2008)"), "9780914098911", Fetcher(None)
    )
    assert found is None and reason == "edition mismatch: citation says 2, the record says '3 edition'"
